recommended_phases.title: Phase 1: Shared infrastructure & base types
recommended_phases.rationale: Foundation layer with zero module dependencies. Establishes BaseEntity, base repository abstract class, error types (AppError, NotFoundError, ValidationError, UnauthorizedError), ValidationResult, pagination types, and the db connection pool. Every other module depends on this.

recommended_phases.title: Phase 2: Employee module
recommended_phases.rationale: Depends only on shared. Provides employee lookup, manager relationship queries, and active-status checks. Needed by balance (for employee validation) and leave (for submitter/manager resolution).

recommended_phases.title: Phase 3: Policy module
recommended_phases.rationale: Depends only on shared. Defines LeaveType enum, LeavePolicy model, and policy lookup methods. Needed by balance (for entitlement rules) and leave (for approval requirements, notice periods).

recommended_phases.title: Phase 4: Audit module
recommended_phases.rationale: Depends only on shared. Implements GP-002 (all state-changing operations write an audit record). LeaveService will call this after every state transition. Built early so it's available when leave orchestration begins.

recommended_phases.title: Phase 5: Notification module
recommended_phases.rationale: Depends only on shared. Handles notification creation for leave lifecycle events (submitted, approved, rejected, cancelled). LeaveService fires these after state transitions.

recommended_phases.title: Phase 6: Balance module
recommended_phases.rationale: Depends on shared, employee, policy. Owns the leave balance ledger — deductBalance, restoreBalance, hasSufficientBalance. LeaveService depends on this for balance validation during submission and restoration on cancellation/rejection.

recommended_phases.title: Phase 7: Leave module — models, repository, service interface
recommended_phases.rationale: Depends on shared, employee, policy, balance, audit, notification. Defines LeaveStatus enum, LeaveRequest model, DTOs, query params, repository interface, and ILeaveService interface. No implementation yet — just the contracts.

recommended_phases.title: Phase 8: Leave module — service implementation
recommended_phases.rationale: Implements ILeaveService with full orchestration: submitLeaveRequest (validates employee, checks policy rules, verifies balance, deducts, audits, notifies), approveLeaveRequest (validates manager, updates status, audits, notifies), rejectLeaveRequest (validates manager, updates status, restores balance, audits, notifies), cancelLeaveRequest (validates ownership, updates status, restores balance, audits, notifies).

recommended_phases.title: Phase 9: Leave module — controller & routes
recommended_phases.rationale: Fastify routes with RBAC enforcement (GP-005) and input validation (GP-003). POST /leaves (submit), PATCH /leaves/:id/approve, PATCH /leaves/:id/reject, PATCH /leaves/:id/cancel, GET /leaves/:id, GET /leaves (employee's own), GET /leaves/pending (manager's pending approvals), GET /leaves/calendar (team calendar).

app_notes:
## Application Layer Design — Leave Management Module

### Layer boundaries

| Layer | Modules | Responsibility |
|-------|---------|----------------|
| **Infrastructure** | `shared/` | DB connection, base repository, error types, validation utilities, pagination |
| **Domain** | `employee/`, `policy/`, `balance/`, `leave/`, `audit/`, `notification/` | Models, repository interfaces, service interfaces |
| **Application** | Service implementations in each module | Business logic, orchestration, cross-module coordination |
| **Presentation** | Controllers + Routes in each module | HTTP handling, input validation (GP-003), RBAC enforcement (GP-005) |

### Dependency direction (all inward)

```
leave ──────────────► balance ──► policy ──► shared
  │                      │          │
  │                      └──► employee ──► shared
  │
  ├──► audit ──────────────────────────► shared
  ├──► notification ───────────────────► shared
  ├──► employee ───────────────────────► shared
  ├──► policy ─────────────────────────► shared
  └──► shared
```

### Key design decisions

1. **LeaveService is the orchestrator** — it coordinates employee validation, policy rule checks, balance deduction/restoration, audit recording (GP-002), and notification dispatch. It never touches the database directly (GP-001).

2. **BalanceService owns the ledger** — `deductBalance` and `restoreBalance` are the only paths to mutate leave balances. LeaveService calls these; no other module does.

3. **PolicyService is read-only at runtime** — policies are configured by HR admins (separate CRUD). The leave workflow only reads policy rules (entitlement, approval requirements, notice periods).

4. **Audit and Notification are fire-and-forget** — LeaveService calls them after state transitions but does not await their completion for the HTTP response. This keeps the approval flow fast.

5. **RBAC is enforced at the controller layer** — controllers check that the requesting user is either the owning employee (for submit/cancel) or the designated manager (for approve/reject) before delegating to the service.

### Phase decomposition rationale

Phases are ordered so that every module's dependencies exist before it is built. Each phase targets ≤5 files to stay within Aider's effective context window. The planner's `maxFilesPerPhase: 5` constraint is respected throughout.
